alert_text: CRITICAL Redis OOM - session-store Redis instance killed by OOM killer. Used memory: 8.2GB/8GB maxmemory
root_cause: Session TTL misconfiguration allowed expired sessions to accumulate, exceeding Redis maxmemory limit and triggering the Linux OOM killer.
resolution_steps: Restarted Redis instance with increased maxmemory to 12GB
Flushed expired session keys using SCAN with TTL filter
Fixed session TTL from 0 (infinite) to 3600 seconds in session-store config
post_mortem_summary: All user sessions were lost when Redis was killed by OOM. A TTL enforcement policy and maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru were configured to prevent recurrence.

alert_text: ERROR Redis connection pool exhausted. Active connections: 256/256. Pending requests queued: 1847
root_cause: API gateway rate limiter held Redis connections open during slow upstream responses, exhausting the connection pool under sustained traffic.
resolution_steps: Increased Redis connection pool size from 256 to 512
Added connection timeout of 500ms to rate limiter Redis client
Deployed circuit breaker around Redis-backed rate limiting with in-memory fallback
post_mortem_summary: API gateway began rejecting requests when Redis connections were exhausted. Connection pool monitoring and fallback rate limiting were implemented.

alert_text: WARN Redis eviction rate spiked to 12000 keys/sec on feature-cache cluster. Cache hit ratio dropped to 31%
root_cause: New product embedding vectors stored in Redis exceeded allocated memory, triggering aggressive LRU eviction of frequently accessed feature vectors.
resolution_steps: Migrated large embedding vectors to dedicated Redis cluster with 32GB allocation
Reduced embedding dimensionality from 768 to 256 for cache storage
Implemented tiered caching with hot features in Redis and cold in disk-backed store
post_mortem_summary: Recommendation latency increased 4x due to cache misses from eviction storms. Embedding storage was separated from operational cache with dedicated memory allocation.

alert_text: SLOW QUERY ALERT: SELECT stock_level FROM inventory WHERE sku IN (...) took 18.7s. Rows examined: 4,200,000
root_cause: Missing composite index on (sku, warehouse_id) forced PostgreSQL into sequential scan when inventory check queries contained more than 100 SKUs.
resolution_steps: Created composite index CREATE INDEX idx_inventory_sku_warehouse ON inventory(sku, warehouse_id)
Added query planner hint to force index usage for IN clauses over 50 items
Implemented batch chunking to limit IN clause to 100 SKUs per query
post_mortem_summary: Cart and checkout flows experienced 15-20 second delays during inventory validation. Index creation reduced query time from 18s to 12ms.

alert_text: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections. Active connections: 200/200
root_cause: Database connection pool leak in the order retry handler kept connections open after transaction rollback, gradually exhausting PostgreSQL max_connections.
resolution_steps: Identified leaked connections using pg_stat_activity showing idle-in-transaction state
Patched order retry handler to properly release connections in finally block
Reduced max_connections per service from 200 to 100 and enabled PgBouncer connection pooling
post_mortem_summary: Order processing halted completely when all database connections were consumed. PgBouncer was deployed and connection lifecycle management was audited across all services.

alert_text: ERROR Deadlock detected: Process 8842 waits for ShareLock on transaction 9918423; blocked by process 8847
root_cause: Concurrent user profile updates and session writes acquired locks in opposite order on the users and sessions tables, causing cyclic deadlocks.
resolution_steps: Reordered lock acquisition to always lock users table before sessions table
Wrapped profile update and session write in a single serializable transaction
Added advisory lock on user_id to serialize concurrent operations per user
post_mortem_summary: Login failures spiked to 8% during peak hours due to deadlocks. Lock ordering convention was documented and enforced across auth-service database operations.

alert_text: ERROR SSL certificate verification failed: certificate has expired. Host: payment-gateway.provider.com:443
root_cause: Third-party payment gateway SSL certificate expired and the payments-api certificate pinning configuration prevented fallback to the renewed certificate.
resolution_steps: Updated certificate pin to include both current and backup certificates from payment provider
Deployed emergency config update to payments-api with new certificate fingerprint
Added certificate expiry monitoring for all external service endpoints
post_mortem_summary: All payment processing failed for 45 minutes during certificate expiry window. Automated certificate expiry alerting with 30-day advance warning was implemented.

alert_text: ERROR TLS handshake timeout after 10s for internal service mesh communication. Affected: 12 upstream services
root_cause: Istio sidecar proxy certificate rotation failed silently, leaving expired mTLS certificates that blocked all inter-service communication.
resolution_steps: Restarted Istio citadel to force certificate reissuance
Rolling restarted all affected service pods to pick up new certificates
Configured Istio certificate rotation monitoring with 24h advance alerting
post_mortem_summary: Complete service mesh communication failure lasted 30 minutes affecting all microservices. mTLS certificate lifecycle monitoring was added to infrastructure observability.

alert_text: WARN p99 latency exceeded 5000ms on /api/v2/products endpoint. Current p99: 8230ms. Normal baseline: 120ms
root_cause: Nginx upstream keepalive connections were being closed by a misconfigured load balancer idle timeout (30s) shorter than the gateway keepalive timeout (60s), forcing TCP reconnections.
resolution_steps: Aligned load balancer idle timeout to 65s to exceed gateway keepalive of 60s
Enabled TCP keepalive probes on load balancer to prevent premature connection closure
Added latency percentile monitoring with automated alerting at p95 and p99 thresholds
post_mortem_summary: Product listing pages loaded slowly affecting conversion rates. Load balancer and gateway timeout alignment was standardized across all environments.

alert_text: CRITICAL p99 search latency at 12400ms. Elasticsearch cluster yellow status. Relocating shards: 47
root_cause: Automated index rollover created 200 small shards overnight, exceeding cluster shard limit and triggering continuous shard rebalancing.
resolution_steps: Increased cluster.max_shards_per_node from 1000 to 2000 as immediate relief
Merged small indices using force merge API to reduce shard count by 60%
Reconfigured ILM policy to rollover at 30GB instead of 1GB to prevent shard proliferation
post_mortem_summary: Search became unusable with 12s response times during shard rebalancing storm. Index lifecycle management policies were revised with shard budget planning.

alert_text: ERROR DiskSpaceMonitor: /data partition 97% full. Estimated time to full: 4 hours. Current usage: 465GB/480GB
root_cause: Product image processing pipeline wrote uncompressed temporary files to /data without cleanup, filling the catalog service data volume.
resolution_steps: Purged 180GB of orphaned temporary image files from /data/tmp/processing
Implemented tmpwatch cron job to auto-delete temp files older than 2 hours
Moved image processing scratch space to ephemeral storage with separate volume mount
post_mortem_summary: Product catalog service risked data partition exhaustion within hours. Temporary file lifecycle management and dedicated ephemeral storage were implemented.

alert_text: CRITICAL WAL segment accumulation detected. pg_wal directory size: 89GB. Disk usage at 94%
root_cause: Stalled replication slot from a decommissioned replica prevented WAL segment recycling, causing unbounded WAL growth on the primary database.
resolution_steps: Identified inactive replication slot using pg_replication_slots view
Dropped stalled replication slot: SELECT pg_drop_replication_slot('replica_old')
PostgreSQL automatically recycled 85GB of WAL segments within minutes after slot removal
post_mortem_summary: Database server nearly ran out of disk due to WAL accumulation from an orphaned replication slot. Automated replication slot monitoring was deployed.

alert_text: ERROR RabbitMQ consumer lag critical. Queue: email-notifications. Messages pending: 847,293. Consumer count: 0
root_cause: Notification worker deployment failed silently due to image pull error, leaving zero consumers running while messages continued to enqueue.
resolution_steps: Fixed container image tag reference in notification-worker deployment manifest
Redeployed notification-worker with correct image, scaling to 8 replicas to drain backlog
Added consumer count alerting with minimum threshold of 2 active consumers per queue
post_mortem_summary: Email notifications were delayed by 6 hours during consumer outage. Deployment validation now checks consumer registration within 60 seconds of rollout.

alert_text: ERROR Kafka consumer group rebalancing loop detected. Group: order-processing. Rebalances in last hour: 47
root_cause: Order processing consumer max.poll.interval.ms was set to 5 minutes but some orders with large item counts took 8+ minutes to process, triggering repeated group rebalances.
resolution_steps: Increased max.poll.interval.ms from 300000 to 900000 for order-processing consumer group
Reduced max.poll.records from 500 to 50 to process smaller batches per poll cycle
Added per-order processing time metrics to identify slow-processing order patterns
post_mortem_summary: Order processing throughput dropped 80% during rebalancing storms. Consumer configuration was tuned and batch size reduced to prevent future rebalance cascades.

alert_text: ERROR JVM heap usage at 96%. GC overhead limit exceeded. Full GC cycles: 14 in last 5 minutes
root_cause: Search service loaded entire product taxonomy tree into memory on each request instead of caching it, causing heap exhaustion under concurrent search load.
resolution_steps: Implemented taxonomy tree caching with 5-minute TTL using Caffeine cache library
Increased JVM heap from 4GB to 8GB as immediate mitigation
Added JVM heap usage alerting at 80% threshold with automatic heap dump capture
post_mortem_summary: Search service crashed repeatedly due to memory exhaustion from uncached taxonomy loading. Object caching and heap monitoring prevented recurrence.

alert_text: WARN Container memory usage: 7.8GB/8GB (97.5%). OOMKill imminent. RSS growing at 50MB/hour
root_cause: Python recommendation service leaked TensorFlow session objects when model hot-reloading failed, accumulating unreleased GPU memory allocations.
resolution_steps: Added explicit tf.Session.close() in model reload error handler
Implemented memory usage watchdog that triggers graceful restart at 90% memory threshold
Configured Kubernetes memory limit to 12GB with proper resource requests for scheduling
post_mortem_summary: Recommendation pods were OOMKilled every 12 hours due to TensorFlow session leaks. Session lifecycle management and proactive memory monitoring were added.

alert_text: ERROR OAuth2TokenService - JWT signature verification failed. KeyID: rsa-key-2024-q3 not found in JWKS endpoint
root_cause: Identity provider rotated JWKS signing keys but auth-service cached the old JWKS for 24 hours, causing all token validations to fail after key rotation.
resolution_steps: Reduced JWKS cache TTL from 24 hours to 5 minutes
Implemented JWKS cache invalidation on signature verification failure with immediate refetch
Added fallback to try all keys in JWKS before rejecting token
post_mortem_summary: All authenticated API calls failed for 20 minutes after IdP key rotation. JWKS caching strategy was revised with shorter TTL and on-failure refresh.

alert_text: ERROR PaymentReconciliation - 342 transactions in PENDING state for >30 minutes. Expected completion: <5 minutes
root_cause: Webhook endpoint for payment provider callbacks was returning 503 due to rate limiting, causing payment status updates to be dropped silently.
resolution_steps: Increased rate limit for /webhooks/payments endpoint from 100 to 1000 req/s
Implemented webhook retry queue to buffer and replay failed webhook deliveries
Added reconciliation job that polls payment provider API for stale PENDING transactions every 5 minutes
post_mortem_summary: Customers saw stuck payment status on 342 orders. Webhook processing capacity was increased and a safety-net reconciliation poller was deployed.

alert_text: ERROR ElasticsearchSyncJob - Bulk index request failed. 2847 documents rejected: mapper_parsing_exception
root_cause: Product data feed included new fields with incompatible types that conflicted with existing Elasticsearch index mapping (string sent for integer price field).
resolution_steps: Identified malformed documents using Elasticsearch rejection logs
Added schema validation layer before Elasticsearch bulk indexing
Reindexed rejected documents after data type correction in upstream feed
post_mortem_summary: 2847 products became unsearchable after sync failure. Input validation was added to catch type mismatches before indexing.

alert_text: WARN Redis cluster node failure detected. Node redis-cluster-03 unreachable. Cluster state: FAIL. Slots affected: 5461-10922
root_cause: Kernel update on redis-cluster-03 host triggered unexpected reboot without draining Redis cluster node, causing slot ownership gap in the cluster.
resolution_steps: Forced cluster failover to promote replica of redis-cluster-03 as new primary
Verified cluster slot coverage restored to 100% using CLUSTER INFO
Implemented pre-reboot drain script for Redis cluster nodes in maintenance playbook
post_mortem_summary: One-third of user sessions became inaccessible during Redis node outage. Maintenance procedures now require cluster-aware node draining before host operations.

alert_text: ERROR SMTPConnectionPool - Connection refused to smtp-relay.internal:587. Consecutive failures: 847
root_cause: Internal SMTP relay crashed due to malformed email with 50MB attachment that exhausted relay memory, taking down the shared email infrastructure.
resolution_steps: Restarted SMTP relay service with increased memory limit from 2GB to 4GB
Added 10MB attachment size limit validation in notification-worker before SMTP submission
Implemented SMTP health check with automatic failover to backup relay endpoint
post_mortem_summary: All email notifications were blocked for 90 minutes while SMTP relay was down. Input validation and relay redundancy were added.

alert_text: ERROR HealthCheck - 5 consecutive health check failures for service: order-service. Removing from load balancer pool
root_cause: Order-service health endpoint performed a deep database connectivity check that started failing when database connection pool was saturated during peak traffic.
resolution_steps: Changed order-service health endpoint to shallow check (process alive + port listening)
Created separate /ready endpoint for deep dependency checks used only by deployment system
Tuned health check intervals from 5s to 10s with failure threshold increased from 3 to 5
post_mortem_summary: Order-service was incorrectly removed from load balancer pool despite being functional. Health check strategy was revised to separate liveness from readiness.

alert_text: CRITICAL Brute force detection triggered. Failed login attempts: 48,000 in 5 minutes from 1,200 unique IPs
root_cause: Credential stuffing attack using compromised credential lists targeted the /auth/login endpoint, bypassing IP-based rate limiting through distributed botnet.
resolution_steps: Enabled CAPTCHA challenge after 3 failed attempts per account
Deployed WAF rule to block credential stuffing patterns based on request fingerprinting
Implemented account lockout with exponential backoff: 1min, 5min, 15min, 1hour
post_mortem_summary: Distributed credential stuffing attack caused elevated auth-service load and some legitimate user lockouts. Multi-layered bot detection was deployed.

alert_text: ERROR CurrencyConversionService - Stale exchange rates detected. Last update: 26 hours ago. Threshold: 1 hour
root_cause: Exchange rate provider API changed authentication scheme from API key header to OAuth2 bearer token, causing silent 401 failures on rate refresh.
resolution_steps: Updated currency service client to use OAuth2 bearer token authentication
Added exchange rate staleness alert with 2-hour threshold
Implemented fallback to secondary exchange rate provider when primary fails
post_mortem_summary: International transactions used stale exchange rates for 26 hours causing financial discrepancies. Provider failover and staleness monitoring were added.

alert_text: ERROR SearchIndexRebuilder - Index rebuild failed at 67%. Elasticsearch disk watermark exceeded on data-node-02
root_cause: Index rebuild process required 2x storage for the new index alongside the old one, but data-node-02 only had 15% free space which was insufficient.
resolution_steps: Expanded data-node-02 EBS volume from 500GB to 1TB
Implemented rolling index rebuild that swaps aliases instead of rebuilding in-place
Added pre-rebuild storage check that validates 2.5x current index size is available
post_mortem_summary: Search index rebuild failed mid-process leaving search results stale for 12 hours. Storage pre-checks and alias-based rebuild strategy were implemented.

alert_text: ERROR InventoryReservationTimeout - Failed to reserve inventory for 127 orders. Timeout after 30s waiting for inventory-db response
root_cause: Long-running analytics query on inventory-db primary acquired a table-level lock that blocked all inventory reservation writes for 4 minutes.
resolution_steps: Killed blocking analytics query using pg_terminate_backend
Moved analytics workload to read replica with statement_timeout set to 60s
Added statement_timeout of 10s on inventory-db primary for non-superuser connections
post_mortem_summary: 127 orders failed during inventory reservation timeout caused by analytics query locking. Workload isolation and query timeouts were enforced.

alert_text: WARN Model serving latency degraded. p95: 890ms (baseline: 45ms). Model: product-similarity-v3. GPU utilization: 12%
root_cause: Model binary was loaded from NFS mount instead of local SSD after pod rescheduling, causing 20x inference latency due to network storage I/O.
resolution_steps: Added initContainer to copy model binary from NFS to local SSD emptyDir volume on pod start
Configured model serving to read from /models/local with NFS as fallback only
Added model load time metric and alert when load exceeds 5 seconds
post_mortem_summary: Recommendation latency spiked 20x after pod rescheduling due to NFS model loading. Local SSD caching of model binaries was implemented.
